commands.review_summary:
The PR makes foreground bash-tool cancellation reject with an AbortError, clears the pending yield timer before killing the process, and adds regression coverage for cancellation races.

PR surface: Source +13, Tests +30. Total +43 across 2 files.

Reproducibility: yes. from source inspection: abort kills the managed process, whose normalized outcome is then resolved as a foreground result on current main. I did not independently execute the current-main failure path, so this is source-reproducible rather than a live reproduction.

target.title: fix(agents): reject with AbortError when tool execution is cancelled
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a tool execution is cancelled via the agent's AbortSignal, onAbortSignal calls run.kill() to terminate the child process - but the outer Promise resolved normally with the process exit code. The agent manager was misled into believing the tool finished normally.

## Root Cause

The process exit handler always called resolve(buildExecForegroundResult(...)) regardless of whether the exit was caused by an abort signal. Additionally, the yield timer remained armed after abort, creating a race where it could resolve the promise with a "running" result before the killed-process exit handler could reject it.

## Fix

1. Added a `toolAborted` flag set by onAbortSignal before calling run.kill()
2. Clear the yield timer in onAbortSignal so it cannot race against the killed-process exit handler
3. In run.promise.then(), check toolAborted first and reject with AbortError instead of resolving

## User Impact

- Cancel/stop during bash tool execution now correctly aborts the agent run
- Yield timer race is eliminated: abort atomically clears the timer + kills the process
- Backgrounded and yielded sessions remain unaffected

## Evidence

### A. Unit Test Results (35/35 passed)

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/bash-tools.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  35 passed (35)
```

### B. Regression Test: Yield Timer Race (new test)

```
 ✓ rejects with AbortError when abort fires before yield window expires
```

This test starts a foreground command with a 60s yield window, triggers abort during execution (via onUpdate), and expects the promise to reject with "Tool execution was aborted" - NOT resolve with a "running" session result.

Before the fix, the yield timer would resolve the promise. After the fix, onAbortSignal clears the timer first.

### C. Code Flow (Before vs After)

```
BEFORE (bug):
  onAbortSignal -> run.kill() -> [yieldTimer still armed -> race!]
  -> process exits -> run.promise.then() -> resolve(...)
  -> agent run treats cancelled tool as successful execution

AFTER (fixed):
  onAbortSignal -> toolAborted=true -> clearTimeout(yieldTimer) -> run.kill()
  -> process exits -> run.promise.then() -> check toolAborted -> reject(AbortError)
  -> agent run correctly aborts
```

### D. Lint + Format

```
$ npx oxlint -c .oxlintrc.json src/agents/bash-tools.exec.ts
  No errors
$ npx oxfmt --check src/agents/bash-tools.exec.ts
  All matched files use the correct format
```

### E. Merge Risk: session-state

The change is scoped to in-flight foreground tool execution only. It does not touch session persistence, SQLite, config, or storage. Backgrounded and yielded sessions return early from onAbortSignal and are unaffected.

## What Changed

- src/agents/bash-tools.exec.ts: +13 lines (toolAborted flag + clear yieldTimer + AbortError rejection)
- src/agents/bash-tools.test.ts: +23 lines (regression test for yield timer race)

Fixes #105681
